tools/prepare_cross_sections/reports/pho.rationale: The 0.7123% p95 difference (1.6582% worst, within its 2% gate) remains the accepted change from the historical Geant4 fitted representation to direct EPICS2023 EPDL; the comparison stays on the historical baseline's domain (Z=1-92, 10 keV-10 MeV). The runtime tables now cover Z=1-98 and 10 keV-20 MeV. Every emitted curve, including Z=93-98 and the 10-20 MeV intervals, meets the generator gates against EPDL (0.1% pointwise, 0.05% for pair production, 0.05% integrated; angular and Rayleigh-CDF gates), re-checked on the emitted tables. Old-vs-new drift inside 10 keV-10 MeV is at most 0.18% per process and 0.10% in total attenuation, from re-selected nodes and repacking when the upper endpoint moved; both representations are within the generator gates against EPDL. The only larger moves are in the pair-production threshold sliver, where pair production is below 1e-6 of total attenuation and under the generator's floor. Independent NIST XCOM checks give photoelectric+Compton+pair agreement within 0.3% for Z=92-98 and within 0.5% at 12-20 MeV.

tools/prepare_cross_sections/reports/sto.accepted_gate: historical stopping, CSDA-range, and deterministic-deposition compatibility
tools/prepare_cross_sections/reports/sto.rationale: The differences are concentrated away from the 12 elements in the historical correction surface and reflect replacing cross-element interpolation, including gas/solid density-effect discontinuities, with direct all-Z NIST ESTAR tables. Historical anchor elements remain close. The per-element affine uint16 encoding adds at most 0.00195% collision and 0.00401% radiative error at the native nodes, negligible relative to both NIST's stated source precision and the accepted migration change. Re-bound 2026-09-23 after the photon extension changed the source lock; the stopping data and this report's measured values are unchanged (only its recorded source-lock hash differs).
